questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the helping verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

These types of questions contain Modal verbs and they should be used correctly as stated below. Modal verbs can be identified by the following:

Can
Could
May
Might
Shall
Should
Will
Would

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + Modal + be + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of sentences containing Modal verbs in Active voice is: Subject + Modal + V1 + Object.

For example:

The issue shall be solved by you. (Passive Voice)

You shall solve the issue. (Active Voice)

From the given options, the sentence that follows the Active voice format is option (b), "The receptionist shall welcome the guests".

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.question: Select the sentence that is expressed in passive voice.
questions.questionHtml: Select the sentence that is expressed in passive voice.

options.html: The results are announced by the principal.

options.html: They are planning a surprise party.

options.html: She cleaned the room yesterday.

options.text: He will organize the meeting.
options.html: He will organize the meeting.

questions.solution:
Option (a): This sentence is in passive voice.

The subject ("results") is receiving the action ("are announced"), and the doer ("principal") is introduced with "by."

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

Option (b): This sentence is in active voice. The subject ("They") performs the action ("are planning").

Option (c): This sentence is in active voice. The subject ("She") performs the action ("cleaned").

Option (d): This sentence is in active voice. The subject ("He") performs the action ("organize").

Note: Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The chef had prepared all the dishes before the guests arrived.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

options.html: All the dishes are prepared by the chef before the guests arrived.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice ("The chef") is changed into the object of the Passive Voice ("by the chef"). Also, the object of the Active Voice ("all the dishes") is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form ['been'] of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Perfect. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Perfect.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + had + V3 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + had + been + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Arya had bought a new horse. (Active Voice)

A new horse had been bought by Arya. (Passive Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice:

· (a) uses simple past ("were prepared")

· (b) uses present perfect ("have been prepared")

· (d) uses simple present ("are prepared")

Therefore, the correct answer is (c): All the dishes had been prepared by the chef before the guests arrived.

Note: V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).
